name: Research helper extra readers: a read-only browser for pages that need JavaScript, and text from videos and podcasts
description: The research helper (F019) can also read public pages that show nothing without JavaScript, logged out, and pull the text out of videos that have captions and podcasts that publish a transcript, so a parent can ask for the main points from a link. The browser is kept read-only in code: no clicking, typing, form filling or uploads. Bot walls and logins stop it.
example: A parent texts a link to a public page that shows nothing without JavaScript and asks what it says about sign-up dates; the helper opens it in the logged-out browser and the parent's own agent relays the dates with the link. Or Tony texts a link to a long video that has captions and asks for the main points.
how: On the research helper (F019) only. (1) Browser: the `browser` tool in the roadmap's sandbox browser container, on its own network with the home network blocked; `sandbox.browser.enabled` for the helper only, `allowHostControl` left false, `browser.evaluateEnabled: false`, the tool named in the helper's tool allow and sandbox tool allow lists. The image is built from a source checkout; if it cannot be built, the browser half is not built, and no host browser is used. (2) House-rules plugin, one rule: for the helper, a short allowlist of read-only browser action names (status, tabs, open, navigate, focus, close, snapshot, text, screenshot); everything else, `act` and `upload` included, is blocked, failing closed. (3) Video and podcast text: a small connector on the Mac mini, allowed to the helper only and denied by name elsewhere, wraps `summarize --extract --json` with `--firecrawl off`, no keys and no transcription fallback, and refuses home-network addresses itself. Planted-page cases join the eval suite.
caveats: Bot walls, logins, CAPTCHAs and two-factor prompts stop it. They are reported, never solved, and the docs say sandboxed browser sessions are more likely to be flagged as bots.

The browser image cannot be built from the npm install; it needs a source checkout. There is no fallback to a browser on the Mac itself: if the image cannot be built, only the video and podcast reader ships.

Read-only means no clicking, typing or scrolling, so a page that shows its content only after a click or a scroll stays unreadable. Allowing scrolling or hovering back later needs a further check written then, with an eval case each.
The action names come from the installed 2026.9.7 browser tool and can change with any update. Blocking by default keeps a new action blocked, but the rule needs its test after every OpenClaw update.

The video and podcast reader runs on the Mac mini outside the address checks that cover the page reader and the browser, and it has third-party extraction fallbacks of its own; the wrapper has to switch those off and check the address itself.
A video without captions or a podcast without a published transcript returns nothing: no transcription is set up.
corrections: The catalog says to 'use the host profile'; because research must stay sandboxed, the browser tool defaults to the sandbox browser, and the host profile needs `agents.defaults.sandbox.browser.allowHostControl: true` plus an explicit host target.

The catalog's install line names the tap formula steipete/tap/summarize (as the bundled skill does); the upstream README opened in this run gives `npm install --global @steipete/summarize` or `brew install summarize`.
unverified: How often the pages a parent cares about block a headless, logged-out browser; not measured.

Whether the blocking check sees the browser call's action name, and whether it is given the helper's own id when the helper runs as a hand-off (T5; the names were read from the tool's schema, not seen in a live call).
Whether script-rendered pages can be read with no waiting, clicking or scrolling.

Whether the sandbox browser gives the helper a working `browser` tool with the top-level `browser.enabled` left false; the sandbox page says it is not required, the browser setup page says the tool needs it.
With open and navigate allowed, whether a link straight to a file is saved into the browser's downloads folder without the download action being called.

What `summarize` returns for a video without captions when no transcription is configured, and which of its flags exist in the installed version (`--youtube auto` appears in the bundled skill; check `summarize --help` after install).
Whether `summarize` can be made to send its calls through the outbound proxy; if not, its firewall rule and the wrapper's own address check are its only limits.
safety: The helper holds no private data, memory or accounts, and its browser never holds a login. Only read-only browser actions pass, in code that fails closed; page scripts are off and the home network is out of reach, so bookings and CAPTCHA boxes stay out of reach. A task handed to it may carry the town and ages, never names or the school.

name: Lights and speakers by text: Hue and Sonos through a memory-less home agent, with a read-only 'still on' check
description: A parent texts Happy to switch Hue rooms and scenes by name, or to play a Sonos favourite, pause the music or set a room's volume, under one hard volume cap enforced in code. Separately, at an evening time Tony sets, he gets a text only if lights or speakers are still on; that check switches nothing. Locks, garage, alarm and gate are never included.
example: A parent texts: 'Downstairs lights off and pause the music.' At the time Tony set, and only if something is on, he gets a text that starts with the job's label and names the lights and the speaker that are still on.
how: Step 1, read-only: a no-model job from the jobs script runs the `openhue` and `sonos` status commands on the Mac mini at the evening time Tony names and texts him only if something is on (`NO_REPLY` otherwise). Step 2, switching: a sandboxed `home` agent with no memory, no web tool and no message tool, on its own capped model key, reached by hand-off from each parent's agent, holds in-house tools that wrap the two command-line programs. Hue: rooms and scenes by name, the bridge key kept in `~/.openhue/config.yaml`. Sonos: favourites, pause and volume, with one hard volume cap in the tool's code (Tony's number); no play-by-search. No quiet hours and no night cap; a room Tony wants left out is left out in the tool's code. The gateway's node process needs the macOS Local Network permission, or `--ip` per speaker. House-rules plugin: no rule; the cap sits inside the Sonos tool. Not built: Home Assistant, the TV, announcements.
caveats: This switches things in the house, so the volume cap is in the tool's code and not in the prompt. The number is Tony's starting value, not a sourced one.
Neither command-line tool is installed, and the bridge and the two speakers come from the 9 Oct scan and were not re-checked.
Favourites only: play-by-search is left out, because auto-playing the first search hit has no content filter.

Every command is two model turns, because the parent's agent hands it to the home agent. Putting the tools on each parent's own agent would be one turn, but that turns on how Tony reads his one-agent-per-permission-set rule and is not done here.
No quiet hours and no night cap: a parent's own late command is carried out. The Hue app can already switch lights at a set time, so the evening text is a nudge, not the switching.
Home Assistant, TV control and spoken announcements are not built. If the Home Assistant VM is ever built for the kids' speaker, routing house devices through it is reconsidered then.
corrections: 'sonoscli is go install only' is wrong: the project's install page recommends Homebrew (a steipete tap) and also offers prebuilt release archives; go install needs Go 1.26 or later. Only the bundled skill's metadata is limited to go install, so Go does not have to be installed on the Mac mini.

'Isolated runs cannot approve' is too strong: the exec approvals doc says approvals from scheduled runs are delivered to connected approval clients (Control UI, the apps) and the run waits, but they never go to chat channels and are denied at once when no such client is connected. For an iMessage-only household the conclusion is unchanged: use a dry-run period, not per-call approval.
unverified: Philips Hue's own local API documentation sits behind a developer login and was not opened; only the OpenHue CLI pages were.
Whether the gateway needs the Local Network permission for plain HTTPS to the bridge; the bundled skills document it only for Sonos discovery.
That the two programs report 'on' states in a form a short script can parse reliably; neither is installed.
That a hand-off to the home agent returns its result to the parent's agent (T4, first tried with the research helper, F019).
That a no-model job run by Happy's scheduler can reach the bridge and the speakers on the home network once the firewall blocks programs by default.
safety: The home agent can change lights and speakers, so it holds no memory, family data, web tool or message tool, and is reached only by a bounded hand-off. Its tools' code offers only named rooms and scenes, favourites, pause and volume under a hard cap, and has no command for locks, garage, alarm or gate. The evening check runs no model and switches nothing.

name: Printing: 'print this' for an attached PDF or photo, and pages Happy wrote
description: A parent texts 'print this' with an attached PDF or photo and it prints on the printer at home, with a cap on copies; Happy can also print a page it has just written at the parent's request, such as the emergency card. This matters mainly when the parent is away from home, since a phone on the home Wi-Fi may already print by itself. Links and ordinary web pages are not printed, and nothing prints by itself.
example: Tony, still at work, texts a form as a PDF with 'print this, one copy', so it is on the printer when he gets home.
how: First the thirty-second check: from an iPhone on the home Wi-Fi, open any PDF, tap Share and then Print, and see whether the printer Tony names appears. Then one print queue is added once on the Mac mini with `lpadmin`. One in-house tool on each parent's own agent calls `lp -d <queue> -n <copies>` on the Mac mini, with the queue fixed and a copies cap in the tool's code. It prints two things only: a PDF or photo the parent attached in that chat (photo and PDF reading, F002, must be on), and a page of plain text Happy wrote in that chat because the parent asked, such as the emergency card (CRT-13). No link is fetched: a parent who has a link saves the file on the phone and attaches it. Nothing prints on a schedule. House-rules plugin: no rule; both limits are inside the tool. One planted-file case joins the eval suite.
caveats: The printer is known only from a network scan and is unconfirmed; that it is a large-format photo printer rests on a web search summary, because the maker's page refused a direct fetch.
If the thirty-second check shows that a phone on the home Wi-Fi can already print, Happy's gain is printing while away from home and printing pages it wrote.
The print queue has not been added, and a driverless queue for this printer has not been tried.
Attached files only: no links and no web pages. Printing or saving a web page stays a two-tap job on the phone.
No page prints by itself on Sunday and there are no chore turns: no chore rota is on record. A parent who wants paper asks Happy to print the week once calendar questions (F009) exist.
A print job cannot be recalled once it is sent.
unverified: Whether a driverless queue created with `lpadmin` works with the printer Tony names; no queue was created.
Whether the printer supports printing from the phones; no first-party page could be opened, so the thirty-second check settles it.
How the print tool gets at a file a parent attached: whether an in-house tool is given the attachment's path on the Mac mini was not tried.
Whether the firewall, once it blocks every program by default, needs a rule for the Mac's print system to reach the printer.
safety: Printing goes to one fixed queue with a copies cap in the tool's code, and only on a parent's own request. With no link fetch, the agent that holds a parent's notes gains no new way to reach an outside address: the only way out added is paper at home. No scheduled job gets the tool.

name: Project check-ins over several days: a saved note and one recurring reminder (Tony only)
description: Tony hands Happy a project with an end date; Happy keeps one project note among his saved notes, and a recurring reminder texts him every few days to check in. When he replies, Happy lists what is still open from the note, and he cancels the reminder when the project is done. It works for Tony only: Jordan's agent cannot create timed jobs.
example: Tony texts: 'Help me plan the garage clean-out by the end of the month, and check in with me every few days.' Every third day he gets 'Garage clean-out: reply status for what is open'; he replies 'status' and Happy lists the open items from the note.
how: No new mechanism, on Tony's agent only. (1) The project note is one of his saved notes (F041): the goal, the end date, decisions and open items. It records only what he typed or confirmed. (2) One ordinary recurring reminder (F007) at a fixed gap, for example every three days, whose text asks him to reply 'status'. It carries no tools, so it cannot read the note. (3) One rule in the agent's instructions: keep the note current, and on 'status' list the open items from it. Tony cancels the reminder when the project is done. A lookup he asks for in chat goes to the research helper (F019). House-rules plugin: no new rule; the reminder passes the rule F007 adds (a text to the asker only, no web address, no tools). Not built: a job that sets its own gap, reads the note or removes itself.
depends_on: F041 saved notes (the project note is one of them)
F007 timed reminders, with its reminder rule in the house-rules plugin (Tony's agent only)
F019 research helper, only for lookups Tony asks for in chat
Tony provides at execution: a first project to try it on, and how often the check-in should come
caveats: Tony only: Jordan's agent cannot create timed jobs, because she is not a command owner.
The check-in text does not list the open items by itself; Tony replies to get them. Happy does not vary the gap, and the reminder is not removed at the end date: he cancels it.
The conversation resets every morning at 04:00, so the project note is the only continuity between days.
The note holds only what Tony typed or confirmed. What a web lookup found stays in the chat until he says what to keep.
No bookings, purchases or invitations are sent: the output is options, links and drafts. A static checklist is still easier in a shared Notes or Reminders list; Happy adds the nudge and the lookups.
safety: No new tool, grant or way out. The note is one of Tony's own saved notes, and the nudge is an ordinary reminder that passes the reminder rule in the house-rules plugin: a text to the asker only, no web address, no tools. Web lookups stay with the memory-less research helper (F019). Nothing on the never list is reachable.
unverified: That a recurring reminder at a fixed gap of days can be created from an iMessage turn under F007's rule (T7 covers creating a reminder at all).
That one note per project is found again by keyword after the 04:00 reset (T6 covers saving and finding a note in general).

sources.title: Automation schedules: dynamic cadence (pacing)
sources.supports: Recurring jobs can carry minimum and maximum pacing bounds set with the pacing flags.

sources.title: Automation payloads: agent-turn options
sources.supports: Jobs an agent creates are limited to the creating turn's tools and the agent cannot widen the stored list.

sources.title: How automations work: isolated run hardening
sources.anchor: may remove only their own job
sources.supports: An isolated run can see and remove only its own job, which is how a finished project ends itself.

sources.title: User model: keep it compact
sources.supports: Cron, sub-agent, group and channel sessions do not get MEMORY.md injected.

sources.title: Standing intents: choose the right intention tier
sources.supports: Long-running aims belong in a maintained Markdown note with a review date, not in clock jobs or triggers.

sources.title: Sub-agent announce: private parent completion
sources.supports: A child result can be returned privately to the parent turn with no automatic channel delivery.

sources.title: Sub-agent tool policy
sources.supports: Sub-agents are hard-denied the gateway, cron, message and session-send tools regardless of allowlists.

sources.title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks (arXiv 2503.14499)
sources.supports: Frontier models at the time of the paper finished only about half of tasks that take a human roughly an hour, which argues for short runs with human check-ins.

sources.title: Automation delivery: delivery modes
sources.supports: A job's delivery mode can be a webhook that posts the finished run to a URL.

sources.title: OpenClaw 2026.9.7 compiled source: automations tool description (delivery)
sources.supports: The text shown to the model says a job's delivery can name a specific chat or post the finished run to a webhook URL.

sources.title: Manage automations: owner and administrator authority
sources.supports: A channel sender listed as a command owner can have the agent list, inspect, update, run or remove any automation on the gateway, whoever created it.

sources.title: Hardened baseline: chat-driven agent turns
sources.supports: Senders who are not owners cannot use the cron or gateway tools whatever the config says.

sources.title: System prompt: long-running-work guidance
sources.supports: OpenClaw's built-in guidance tells an agent to handle future follow-up, such as checking back later and recurring work, with scheduled jobs; together with the vendor's advice to keep a longer aim in a project note with a review date (already on the item) this is the feature's pattern.

adds: From AUT-03 (Self-paced watch loop (/loop and paced automations)): The /loop command runs on the same scheduling tool and needs the same prerequisites as AUT-01's check-ins: the delivery pin extended to automations add and update with webhooks refused, cron.triggers.enabled false, and owner status. If that grant is ever made, /loop works for an owner too; house rule is an explicit interval of 15 minutes or more and a stop condition, and since it sees only search snippets, page watching stays with F029. The round-1 review of OCL-06 takes /loop out of that entry, so this note is where /loop is described.
review_notes: All nine sources check out, but the safety case has a hole: the `automations` tool this feature depends on can set a job's delivery to any chat or to a webhook URL, and command-owner status lets either parent's agent read and edit the other's jobs. The project note also collides with the F041 rule that tainted turns cannot write memory. Value lowered to 3.
